blocks.content: My apartment has one window that faces east.
6:15. The light gets there before the alarm does.

I keep the space a certain way. Not because anyone asked me to — it just helps me think. Paints sorted by temperature on the shelf above my desk, warm left, cool right. Brushes standing handle-up in three mason jars, widest to narrowest. Canvases leaned against the wall in order of size. When I come back from a run, or a commission, or just a long day, I need to be able to see where everything is and know nothing moved.

My mom came over last spring. She looked around carefully before she said anything — which meant she'd already taken it all in before she looked. She asked, in the specific tone of someone who means something else, if I was okay.
I told her I was. She moved a brush on my desk while we were talking — just a couple inches, not on purpose — and I noticed it the moment she did. I didn't say anything.

The sketchbook on the desk is the one exception. It's always open. The cover has pencil smudges and a coffee ring from last year that landed at an angle I found compositionally interesting and couldn't bring myself to wipe away. The pages inside are the only part of my life I don't try to keep orderly.
I pulled on my running clothes. Drank half a glass of water at the sink.
